## What it is for

The Ogg Opus file reader miniaudio's libopus decoding backend (`Vendor/miniaudio/VENDOR.md`,
`extras/decoders/libopus/miniaudio_libopus.c`) opens Opus files with, over libogg (`Vendor/libogg/VENDOR.md`) and libopus
(`Vendor/libopus/VENDOR.md`): M23's Ogg Opus import and playback (A-OPUS, `Docs/Decisions/0034-m23-contract.md` decision
16). No first-party code includes its header. The engine registers the backend for `Audio/AudioDecoder` and the
`AudioEngine`'s resource manager (`Audio/Private/MiniaudioOpus.h`), asks it for 16-bit samples (`op_read`), and checks
an Ogg Opus file's pages and identification header before opusfile reads it (one logical stream, channel mapping family
0 or 1).

## Build configuration (`premake5.lua`)

- Files: `libopusfile_la_SOURCES` of upstream's `Makefile.am` (`src/info.c`, `src/internal.c`, `src/internal.h`,
  `src/opusfile.c`, `src/stream.c`) and `include/opusfile.h`. Include directories `include`, `../libogg/include` and
  `../libopus/include` (the headers `opusfile.h` includes).
- Defines: `OP_FIXED_POINT` (upstream's `--enable-fixed-point`, matching libopus's `FIXED_POINT` build), with the float
  API kept (upstream's `--disable-float` is not given, so `op_read_float`, which miniaudio's backend references, links).
  In fixed point opusfile decodes 16-bit samples with `opus_multistream_decode`, applies the header's output gain inside
  libopus (`OPUS_SET_GAIN`, integer arithmetic), never dithers, and `op_read_float` converts each sample as
  `(1.0F / 32768) * x`, exactly; the engine reads `op_read`'s samples. `OP_FIXED_POINT` is read by `src/internal.h`
  only, never by `opusfile.h`. `OP_ENABLE_ASSERTIONS`, `OP_DISABLE_FLOAT_API` and `OP_ENABLE_HTTP` stay undefined, as
  upstream's defaults leave them. `HAVE_CONFIG_H` is not used: the switches an autotools `config.h` would hold are given as defines, and only
  `OP_FIXED_POINT` is set.
- C dialect and warnings: the compiler defaults (upstream sets neither); the library compiles without warnings under
  MSVC 14.51 at the workspace's `/W3` for vendored code, with no define or option to silence one.
- Linux: `pic "On"`. Debug: `symbols "on"`; Release: `optimize "on"`, `symbols "on"`; Dist: `optimize "full"`,
  `symbols "off"`.
- The Linux and macOS builds are generated by the portability stage and never compiled (ADR 0028 decision 10).

## Consumer usage

```lua
-- Dependencies.lua: UseOpusFile(), called by UseMiniaudio() right after it links miniaudio: links only.
filter { "kind:ConsoleApp or WindowedApp or SharedLib" }
    links { "opusfile" }
filter {}
```

Vendored consumers (`Vendor/miniaudio`) add `../opusfile/include`, `../libogg/include` and `../libopus/include` to their
include directories and include `<opusfile.h>` with no defines. `Scripts/CheckBuildConfig.py`'s family for the project
is `OP_*`, `OP_FIXED_POINT` excepted as the library's own (`VENDOR_PRIVATE_DEFINES`), so a consumer defines none, and
`Scripts/Lint.py` bans defining `OP_*` in first-party source.

## Updating

1. Download the release tag's archive from `https://github.com/xiph/opusfile/archive/refs/tags/<tag>.tar.gz`, record
   its SHA-256 and size, and extract it into an empty directory.
2. Replace the kept files above and diff `Makefile.am` and `configure.ac` (sources, switches and their defaults)
   against `premake5.lua`.
3. Rebuild Debug, Release and Dist (no warning), run the `AudioDecoder*` and `AudioImporter*` unit cases in Debug and
   Release (the Opus digest among them), and update this file.
